title: Napoleon Dynamite
tagline: Tots in the pocket. Lunch sorted.

Preston High CafeteriaNapoleon DynamiteTots in the pocket. Lunch sorted.Every recipe serves 4.
    StartersMainsSweetsDrinks
    StartersPocket totsHomemade grated potato tots fried until crispHow to make it800g potatoes1 tsp onion powder1 tsp fine salt2 L vegetable oilParboil the whole potatoes, then cool.Grate, squeeze dry and season with salt and onion powder.Shape into little cylinders and freeze.Fry in the vegetable oil at 180°C in batches until golden and crisp all over.Idaho potato skinsCrisp potato skins with cheddar and bacon, sour cream and chivesHow to make it8 small potatoes30g butter, melted150g cheddar, grated4 rashers of bacon150g sour cream1 small bunch chivesBake the potatoes at 200°C until tender.Halve and scoop out most of the flesh. Cook the bacon until crisp and crumble.Brush with butter and crisp at 220°C.Fill with cheddar and bacon and bake until melted.Top with sour cream and chives.MainsNapoleon's quesadillaFlour tortillas with cheddar and Monterey Jack, pan crisped, salsa and sour creamHow to make it8 flour tortillas150g cheddar, grated150g Monterey Jack, grated3 tomatoes, diced200g sour creamFill the tortillas with the grated cheddar and Monterey Jack and fold in half.Cook in a dry pan over medium heat until golden and melted, turning once.Serve with diced tomato salsa and sour cream.Uncle Rico's rump steak and cornThe steak Rico throws at Napoleon from the porchHow to make itAs written, serves 4Rump steak seared hard in a smoking pan, rested and sliced, with corn on the cob in paprika butter and a pile of crispy smashed potatoes.Season 4 rump steaks (about 220g each) with salt and pepper 30 minutes ahead.Boil 800g baby potatoes until tender, smash flat on an oiled tray and roast at 220°C for 25 minutes.Boil 4 corn cobs for 6 minutes and roll in 50g butter mixed with 1 tsp paprika.Sear the steaks in a smoking hot pan with 1 tbsp oil for 3 minutes a side for medium rare, rest 5 minutes, slice and serve with the corn and potatoes.SweetsPedro's campaign piñata cakeHollowed butter cake filled with candy, covered in bright buttercream stripesHow to make it450g butter, soft200g caster sugar4 eggs250g self-raising flour100ml full cream milk200g lollies400g icing sugar1 tsp food colouring (assorted)Heat the oven to 170°C and grease an ovenproof bowl. Beat half the butter with the sugar, then the eggs.Fold in the flour and milk, pour into the bowl and bake.Cool completely.Hollow out the centre and fill with the lollies.Beat the remaining butter with the icing sugar, split it into portions and tint each with a different food colouring, then cover the cake in bright stripes.DrinksFFA blue ribbon chocolate malt shakeChocolate ice cream and malt blended with milk, topped with cream and dark chocolateHow to make it600ml full cream milk, cold6 scoops of chocolate ice cream4 tbsp malted milk powderpinch of salt150ml thickened cream20g dark chocolateChill four tall glasses.Blend the milk, ice cream, malt powder and salt until thick and smooth.Whip the cream to soft peaks.Pour into the glasses, spoon on cream and grate chocolate over each.
